located_point.method: Wikidata starting point retained. Renders at that point and at the coordinate printed for 'Juni Kurna' in Bhan and Ajithprasad's Shikarpur 2007-2008 report (23.95354, 69.75566) show fields, drainage lines and the modern village; the citadel and the roughly 220 m outer enclosure of the plan could not be outlined, so the mound was not located independently.

notes: Plan only. The scan is about 100 dpi and its legend and scale labels are illegible. The straight double and single lines enclosing the area east of the citadel were read as the outer fortification that the report text describes; the rounded line bundles around the citadel look like contours and were not measured. The drawn enclosure is not rectangular: its east side (theta -15.7) and its south and north sides (-9.1, -9.9, -8.5) differ by about 6.6 degrees, so they cannot share a system, and the north segments lie about 236 m from the south wall, beyond the 200 m neighbour distance. The rule therefore makes the single east wall (223 m) the main system. We prefer the three east-west wall lines as the better representative, length-weighted theta about -9.2 degrees over 255 m, because they agree with each other on both sides of the enclosure. The east line of the east double wall failed to fit and is not used.
